title: a firstmate brief recorded for a round still reaches the worker when the branch head changed only by a merge of its base
acceptance: Why. On 2026-10-05 firstmate recorded the T-192 round-2 brief with `bash bin/lib/fm-evidence.sh brief --repo . --project firstmate-workflow --task T-192 --round 2 --head 7efe000… --file state/briefs/T-192.r2.md`. Before the worker started, the autopilot's branch update (T-190) merged main into the branch, so the round's head was 7cd27ca, a merge of main on top of 7efe000 with the task diff unchanged. `Store.brief(round, head)` (bin/lib/fm_evidence.py:238-241) matches only the exact head, so `build` in bin/lib/fm_context_pack.py:231-232 found no brief, the pack recorded 'missing authorized local brief for exact project/task/round/head' (:350-351), the prompt said 'Unavailable; see coverage warnings.' (:393) and the worker started without its instructions. Firstmate had to kill the round, re-record the brief for 7cd27ca and relaunch. Since T-190 the autopilot updates branches whenever main moves, so this race is routine, not rare. Gate 7 already accepts a review verdict across a merge of the base with the same patch (bin/lib/fm_evidence.py, `gate`, the `record['head'] != args.head` branch); the brief lookup has no such rule.

What the worker sees. When a brief is carried, `build` uses its text exactly like an exact brief (the coverage checks at fm_context_pack.py:48-120 and the `captain:` check at :359 read the same text), and the prompt section '# Approved local brief' starts with one line before the brief text: `Written for head <H1>; carried to <H2> because the branch only merged <base> since then and the task's change is unchanged.` No 'missing authorized local brief' gap is recorded. The pack record appended at :392 is unchanged in shape. When no brief is found exactly and a same-round authorized firstmate brief exists for some other head but fails the carry rule, the gap text becomes `missing authorized local brief for exact project/task/round/head (a brief for this round exists for head <H1>, but <reason>)` where <reason> is one fixed phrase per failed condition: `it is not an ancestor of this head`, `the base ref <B> is unavailable`, `non-merge commits follow it`, `the task's change differs`, or `it could not be checked`; with no such candidate the gap text stays exactly 'missing authorized local brief for exact project/task/round/head'. Existing assertions that search for the substring 'missing authorized local brief' (tests/lib/context_pack_integration.py:122, tests/external-reviews.test.sh:286) keep passing.

Base ref freshness. In bin/fm-worker.sh, immediately before the `python3 … fm_context_pack.py` call (:1165), when `$PR` is non-empty, run the same best-effort fetch the round already uses elsewhere: `git fetch -q origin "+refs/heads/$BASE:refs/remotes/origin/$BASE" 2>/dev/null || true` (compare :576 and :1020). A failed fetch is not an error; a stale or missing base ref only makes the carry fail closed through rule (b) or (c). No other fm-worker.sh behaviour changes, and the call's arguments are unchanged.

Docs, edited in place (T-189 rule; nothing appended at the end of design.md):
- design/design.md §15.5 'Immutable pins and authoritative heads', the paragraph beginning 'The worker's bounded context pack supplements its approved local brief' (about :5111): add that an approved brief is bound to project, task, round and head, and that the pack carries a firstmate brief to a later head only when that head adds nothing but merges of the base (H1 ancestor, no non-merge commits outside the base, same patch-id and file list), stating the head it was written for; any other head change needs a new brief, as gate 7 needs a new review for a changed patch.
- skills/firstmate/SKILL.md rule 6 under '## Process rules (2026-09-25)' (the paragraph starting 'A worker round needs a brief, not a symptom', about :479-498): one sentence that a brief recorded for a round still applies after the autopilot merges the base into the branch, so firstmate does not re-record it for that head; it records a new brief when the round number changes or the branch changed in any other way.

Callers and mirrors (grep of `store.brief`, `.brief(`, `missing authorized local brief`, `Approved local brief`): bin/lib/fm_context_pack.py:231 (the only production caller of `Store.brief`) and :351/:393; tests/lib/context_pack_integration.py:31, :109-123; tests/lib/local_round_records.py:24-35; tests/external-reviews.test.sh:245-286 (FM_EXTERNAL fixture; its brief is at the exact head, so it is unaffected; the carry runs the same way for external projects because it uses only the round's own git tree); bin/lib/fm_autopilot_loop.py:186-197 reads brief records only to clear asks and is not changed. bin/lib/fm_evidence.py and fm-evidence.sh are not changed: the recorded brief keeps its exact head.

In flight. The change affects only how a new round's context pack is built. Briefs already recorded keep their exact head and still match exactly; a round already running keeps the prompt it was built with. After this merges, a brief recorded for a round reaches the worker even if the autopilot merged main into the branch between recording and launch; firstmate still records a new brief when the round number changes or the branch changed in any other way. External projects behave the same, since the carry reads only the round's git tree.

Workers do not run the suites. Evidence is the required GitHub check and the six gates. Fail-first is expected from tests/context-pack.test.sh: cases (1)-(5) above are red on base and green on head; cases (6) and (7) and every existing assertion in tests/context-pack.test.sh, tests/local-round-records.test.sh and tests/external-reviews.test.sh stay green on both.
